settings.question: What's the difference between an A/T, H/T, and M/T tire?
settings.answer: A/T (all-terrain) is the daily-driver truck tire — handles gravel, light off-road, and snow with 3PMSF rating, while staying quiet on pavement. H/T (highway-touring) prioritizes on-road comfort and tread life over off-road grip. M/T (mud-terrain) is aggressive off-road rubber for serious gravel, mud, and rocks — loud on pavement and shorter tread life. Most Calgary truck owners run A/T.

settings.question: Do I need LT-rated tires for my half-ton truck?
settings.answer: Not always. Most half-ton trucks (F-150, RAM 1500, Silverado 1500) come with passenger (P-metric) tires from the factory and are fine for normal use. LT-rated (light-truck) tires have stronger sidewalls and higher load ratings — worth the upgrade if you tow heavy, haul payload, or run gravel back roads. Three-quarter and one-ton trucks should always run LT.

settings.question: Are 3PMSF A/T tires good enough for Calgary winter?
settings.answer: For most truck and SUV drivers — yes. A 3PMSF-rated all-terrain (BFGoodrich KO3, Toyo Open Country A/T III, Bridgestone Dueler A/T ASCENT) meets Alberta's winter-tire mandate for Highway 93 and the Trans-Canada. They're not quite as grippy on packed ice as a dedicated winter tire like Blizzak, but for daily Calgary city driving they handle the cold and snow well.

settings.question: How long do truck tires last?
settings.answer: Premium A/T tires (BFGoodrich KO3, Michelin LTX A/T 2) carry 80,000 km warranties. H/T touring tires (Defender LTX M/S, Open Country H/T II) carry up to 100,000 km. M/T mud-terrain tires wear faster — 40,000–60,000 km is typical. Heavy payload, towing, and aggressive off-road use shorten life. Rotate every 8,000–12,000 km to even out wear.

settings.text: C, D, E, and F ratings correspond to maximum load capacity. A heavy half-ton hauling payload needs Load Range E; a daily-driver Tacoma can run Load Range C or D.
Most premium A/T tires (KO3, Open Country A/T III, Wildpeak A/T Trail) carry the 3PMSF symbol — legal for Alberta's Oct 1 – Apr 30 winter-tire mandate on Highway 93 and the Trans-Canada.

settings.lead: Wider tires don't always mean better off-road
settings.text: Narrower tires cut through snow and mud better; wider tires float on softer surfaces. The right width depends on what you actually drive on most.
If you tow heavy, you need higher load range, stiffer sidewalls, and possibly a dedicated towing tire. Don't run a comfort H/T on a trailer-heavy summer.

settings.heading: Picking the right truck tire for Calgary
settings.intro:
Half-ton trucks are the most-driven vehicles in Calgary, but the tire decision varies wildly based on how you use yours. Daily-driver F-150 commuting to work? An H/T or quiet A/T like the Dueler A/T ASCENT works. Half-ton hauling materials to a job site? Step up to a Load Range E A/T like the KO3. Tundra or RAM 2500 towing through the mountains? You need LT-rated rubber and to think about the towing load.

Here's what we factor in when quoting truck tires:
settings.outro: Not sure which category fits how you drive? Send us your year/make/model + your typical driving pattern (city / job site / trailers / off-road) and we'll quote the right tire — not just the most expensive one.
